description: Open and close are equal, leaving almost no body. Buyers and sellers finished in balance, which signals indecision.
Open, high and close are at the same level with a long lower wick. Sellers drove price down but buyers pushed it all the way back. Bullish after a decline.
Open, low and close are at the same level with a long upper wick. Buyers drove price up but sellers pushed it all the way back. Bearish after an advance.

A doji with long upper and lower wicks. Price swung widely in both directions and closed where it opened, showing strong indecision. Called a Rickshaw Man when the body sits in the middle of the range.
A small body with upper and lower wicks longer than the body. Neither buyers nor sellers took control.
A long green candle with no wicks: it opens at the low and closes at the high. Buyers controlled the whole session. Also known as White Marubozu or Green Marubozu.
A long red candle with no wicks: it opens at the high and closes at the low. Sellers controlled the whole session. Also known as Black Marubozu or Red Marubozu.
A small body at the top of the range with a lower wick at least twice the body. After a decline, it shows buyers rejecting lower prices. Called a Takuri Line when the lower wick is especially long.
A small body at the bottom of the range with a long upper wick. After a decline, it shows buyers starting to test higher prices.
Shaped like a hammer (small body near the top, long lower wick) but appears after an advance. It warns that selling pressure is building.
A small body at the bottom of the range with a long upper wick, appearing after an advance. Buyers pushed up but sellers rejected the higher prices.
A red candle followed by a larger green candle whose body completely covers the red body. Buyers have overwhelmed sellers. Also known as Bullish Engulfing Pattern.
A green candle followed by a larger red candle whose body completely covers the green body. Sellers have overwhelmed buyers. Also known as Bearish Engulfing Pattern.
A long red candle followed by a small green candle whose body sits inside the red body. Selling momentum is fading.
A long green candle followed by a small red candle whose body sits inside the green body. Buying momentum is fading.
A green candle and a red candle with matching highs after an advance. Price fails at the same level twice, suggesting resistance. Also known as Tweezers Top.
A red candle and a green candle with matching lows after a decline. Price holds the same level twice, suggesting support. Also known as Tweezers Bottom.
A green candle, then a red candle that opens above the prior high and closes below the midpoint of the green body. A bearish reversal signal. Also known as Dark Cloud.
A red candle, then a green candle that opens below the prior low and closes above the midpoint of the red body. A bullish reversal signal. Also known as Piercing Pattern.
Three long green candles in a row, each opening inside the previous body and closing near its high. Strong, steady buying. Also known as Three Advancing White Soldiers.
Three long red candles in a row, each opening inside the previous body and closing near its low. Strong, steady selling. Also known as Three Advancing Black Crows.
A long red candle, a small-bodied candle that gaps lower, then a long green candle that closes well into the first body. A bullish reversal.
A long green candle, a small-bodied candle that gaps higher, then a long red candle that closes well into the first body. A bearish reversal.
A morning star whose middle candle is a doji. The doji shows sellers are exhausted, making the reversal signal stronger. Also known as Morning Doji Star.
An evening star whose middle candle is a doji. The doji shows buyers are exhausted, making the reversal signal stronger. Also known as Evening Doji Star.
A bullish harami followed by a third green candle that closes above the first candle's open, confirming the reversal.
A bearish harami followed by a third red candle that closes below the first candle's open, confirming the reversal.
A bullish engulfing followed by a third green candle that closes higher still, confirming the reversal.
A bearish engulfing followed by a third red candle that closes lower still, confirming the reversal.
A long red candle, a doji that gaps below it with no wick overlap, then a green candle that gaps back above the doji. A rare, strong bullish reversal. Also known as Abandoned Baby Bottom.
A long green candle, three small red candles that stay within its range, then a long green candle closing at a new high. The uptrend continues. Also known as Rising Three.
A long red candle, three small green candles that stay within its range, then a long red candle closing at a new low. The downtrend continues. Also known as Falling Three.
A red candle followed by a green candle that gaps above the red candle's open. A sudden, strong shift from selling to buying. Also known as Bullish Kicking.
A green candle followed by a red candle that gaps below the green candle's open. A sudden, strong shift from buying to selling. Also known as Bearish Kicking.

A long green candle, a gap up, three small candles drifting lower while staying above the first candle's midpoint, then a long green candle to a new high. A bullish continuation. Also known as Rising Mat or Bullish Mat Hold.

A long green candle that opens at its low and closes near its high, usually after a decline. Buyers took control from the first trade. Also known as Bullish Belt Hold Line or White Opening Shaven Bottom.

A long red candle that opens at its high and closes near its low, usually after an advance. Sellers took control from the first trade. Also known as Bearish Belt Hold Line or Black Opening Shaven Head.
A small body with very long upper and lower wicks. Price swung hard both ways and went nowhere, a sign the market has lost direction. Also known as High-Wave Candle.

Open, high, low and close are all the same, drawn as a flat dash. There was almost no trading range at all, showing extreme indecision or a very thin market. Also known as Four-Price Doji or Flat Line.
A long red candle followed by a doji that gaps below its body. Selling has stalled and a bullish reversal may follow if the next candle confirms. Also known as Doji Star Bottom.
A long green candle followed by a doji that gaps above its body. Buying has stalled and a bearish reversal may follow if the next candle confirms. Also known as Doji Star Top.
A long red candle followed by a doji that sits inside its body. A stronger form of the bullish harami, showing selling pressure has dried up.
A long green candle followed by a doji that sits inside its body. A stronger form of the bearish harami, showing buying pressure has dried up.

A long red candle, then a green candle that gaps down but rallies to close at the same level as the red close. Buyers erased the gap and met sellers head on. Also known as Bullish Meeting Lines or Bullish Counterattack Lines.

A long green candle, then a red candle that gaps up but falls to close at the same level as the green close. Sellers erased the gap and met buyers head on. Also known as Bearish Meeting Lines or Bearish Counterattack Lines.
A long red candle, then a small green candle that opens lower and closes right at the prior low. The bounce is weak and the downtrend usually continues. Also known as On-Neck Line.
A long red candle, then a green candle that opens lower and closes just inside the red body. The bounce barely makes progress and the downtrend usually continues. Also known as In-Neck Line.
A long red candle, then a green candle that opens lower and closes well into the red body but below its midpoint. Buyers fought back but not enough to reverse the trend. Also known as Thrusting Line.
In an uptrend, a red candle is followed by a green candle that opens at the same price as the red open and rallies. The dip is rejected and the uptrend continues.
In a downtrend, a green candle is followed by a red candle that opens at the same price as the green open and falls. The bounce is rejected and the downtrend continues.
Two red candles that close at the same price after a decline. Sellers could not push the close any lower, which marks a support level.
Two green candles that close at the same price after an advance. Buyers could not push the close any higher, which marks a resistance level.
A long red candle followed by a smaller red candle whose body sits inside the first body. Selling is losing force, hinting at a bullish reversal. Also known as Bullish Homing Pigeon.
A long green candle followed by a smaller green candle whose body sits inside the first body. Buying is losing force, hinting at a bearish reversal. Also known as Bearish Homing Pigeon.
Two green candles with a gap between them, then a red candle that closes inside the gap without filling it. The gap holds as support and the uptrend continues. Also known as Bullish Tasuki Gap.
Two red candles with a gap between them, then a green candle that closes inside the gap without filling it. The gap holds as resistance and the downtrend continues. Also known as Bearish Tasuki Gap.
A long green candle, a small red candle that gaps up, then a larger red candle that engulfs it but stays above the first close. Buyers are struggling to hold the gap.
A long green candle, a small red candle that gaps up, then a red candle that opens higher and closes deep inside the first green body. A bearish reversal after an advance.
Three green candles with shrinking bodies and growing upper wicks. The uptrend is still rising but running out of strength.
Two long green candles followed by a small green candle at the top. Also called the stalled pattern, it shows buyers hesitating after a strong run. Also known as Stalled Pattern or Stalled Candle.
Three red candles with shrinking bodies and rising lows, the last a small marubozu inside the prior range. A rare sign that selling is exhausted.
A long red candle, a red candle with a long lower wick that sets a new low, then a small green candle below it. A rare bottom showing sellers failed to hold the new low.
A red candle, a green candle, then another red candle that closes at the same price as the first. The matching closes mark a support level. Also known as Bullish Stick Sandwich.
Three dojis in a row where the middle one gaps below the others. A rare sign of exhaustion at the bottom of a decline. Also known as Tri-Star Bottom.
Three dojis in a row where the middle one gaps above the others. A rare sign of exhaustion at the top of an advance. Also known as Tri-Star Top.
A long green candle, a doji that gaps above it with no wick overlap, then a red candle that gaps back below the doji. A rare, strong bearish reversal. Also known as Abandoned Baby Top.
Three long red candles where each opens at the prior close. A stronger form of three black crows showing relentless selling. Also known as Doji Three Crows.
A green candle, then two similar green candles that gap up and open at about the same price. The gap holds and the uptrend continues. Also known as Upside Gap Side-by-Side White Lines.
Two green candles with a gap between them, then a red candle that opens in the second body and closes in the first, filling the gap. A pause in an uptrend. Also known as Upside Gap Three.
Two red candles with a gap between them, then a green candle that opens in the second body and closes in the first, filling the gap. A pause in a downtrend. Also known as Downside Gap Three.
Two candles with a gap between the first high and the second low. The gap, or window, often acts as support as the uptrend continues. Also known as Gap Up or Upside Gap.
Two candles with a gap between the first low and the second high. The gap, or window, often acts as resistance as the downtrend continues. Also known as Gap Down or Downside Gap.
Three falling red candles, then one long green candle that opens below the last close and closes above the first open, wiping out the whole decline. Also known as Bullish Three-Line Strike.
Three rising green candles, then one long red candle that opens above the last close and closes below the first open, wiping out the whole advance. Also known as Bearish Three-Line Strike.
Two red marubozu, a red candle that gaps down with an upper wick into the prior body, then a red candle that engulfs it entirely. A rare sign that selling is climaxing.
Three falling red candles, a fourth red candle with a long upper wick, then a green candle that gaps up. Buyers are finally stepping in after a steady decline.
A long red candle, a gap down, three small candles drifting lower, then a long green candle that closes inside the gap. The decline loses steam and reverses.
A long green candle, a gap up, three small candles drifting higher, then a long red candle that closes inside the gap. The advance loses steam and reverses.
